12:59 PM EDT (17:59 BST) - "Oil and fuel exports near prewar level with alternate routes, data firm says"
Alternate shipping routes have restored Gulf oil and fuel exports to near prewar volumes. Data firm Kpler reports approximately 21.8 million barrels per day shipped weekly versus the 23.3 million baseline before conflict. Matt Smith, Kpler's commodity research director, stated: "We are getting closer to the norm, we are not at pre-conflict levels, but we are getting close to there."

12:32 PM EDT (17:32 BST) - "U.K. believes Iran 'played a part' in incident near RAF Fairford base used by U.S. forces, prime minister says"
British PM Andy Burnham confirmed to the BBC that Iran "played a part" in a weekend incident at RAF Fairford, which hosts U.S. warplanes conducting strikes on Iran. Five British nationals were arrested Sunday on terrorism suspicion; all were released on bail Monday.

[Rendered as "Lebanese President Nawaf Salam" - NB Nawaf Salam is Lebanon's PRIME MINISTER; likely a rendering error, verify before use] and Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi met Senate Foreign Relations Committee members. Raggi stated discussions "focused on the government's efforts to restore Lebanon's sovereignty and extend state authority across its entire territory."

11:12 AM EDT (16:12 BST) - "Iran-backed Iraqi militias say they do not plan to disarm as U.S. leaves"
Kataeb Hezbollah spokesman Jaafar al-Husseini stated: "the Islamic Resistance declares that it is not bound by any timetable or agreement that any governmental or political party has spoken of."

10:18 AM EDT (15:18 BST) - "3 tankers hit Tuesday in Strait of Hormuz, U.K. naval agency says"
The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations center reported unknown projectiles struck three vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on September 29, including a crude oil tanker and LNG tanker.
